thesis: Space can be physically real without being an ultimate container or fully represented by cognition.
role: Separates spatial ontology, physical geometry, representation and access.

ideas.statement: Operational success does not settle whether space is container, relation or condition of experience.
Emergent spatial relations may be real, but reconstructing an analogue is not proof of the universe’s substrate.
Geometry does not exhaust practical accessibility; maps select whose obstacles count.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Relativity makes geometry dynamical, while internal curvature needs no outside room.
Neighborhood intervention findings vary with age and exposure.
The lesson is methodological. Understanding a concept may require abandoning the image that helped us learn it. A good metaphor is temporary support, not an obligation imposed on reality.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Entanglement and causal-set proposals are restricted research programs, not confirmation that everything is information.

audit.notes: Read every unit; fictional examples and limits retained. Structural transitions excluded from ranking.
